note: Machine-checkable physics-settings rules for Geant4 studies, applied by scripts/check_geant4_study.py spec. Each rule says only when to take care and what to read; it is not a recommendation table. Sources are Geant4 11.4.3 upstream paths (tag v11.4.3, commit 2ee379e6843e55b9c6bbb835d2a2b03cc998fef0; prefix geant4:) or the PDG review; a rule without a source is refused by the checker. Version-matched 11.4 builds of the Physics List Guide and the Book for Application Developers were not found (only dev builds), so the upstream source is the cited authority.
conditions_help: a condition is {all: [...]} or {any: [...]} of {field, op, value}; op is eq, ne, in, not_in, lt, le, gt, ge, exists, missing; field is a dotted path into the study spec, with the derived fields derived.em_only, derived.min_thickness_mm, derived.pai_requested, derived.step_limits, derived.cut_scan_values, derived.hadronic_list

rules.concern: below 20 MeV the data-driven neutron models (ParticleHP, G4NDL) are only in the _HP, _HPT and _AllHP lists and the Shielding family; any other list uses G4NeutronInelasticXS and a cascade model there
rules.read: the hadronic inelastic constructor of the chosen list; the _HP variants register G4ParticleHPInelastic with SetMaxEnergy(20 MeV) and need the G4NDL dataset (G4NEUTRONHPDATA)

source.document: geant4:source/physics_lists/constructors/hadron_inelastic/src/G4HadronPhysicsQGSP_BIC_HP.cc (G4ParticleHPInelastic, SetMaxEnergy(20*CLHEP::MeV)); geant4:source/physics_lists/lists/src/G4PhysListFactory.cc (list names; Shielding is built with "HP"); geant4:cmake/Modules/G4DatasetDefinitions.cmake (G4NDL, ENVVAR G4NEUTRONHPDATA)

rules.concern: in a thin layer the energy-loss fluctuation model shapes the distribution (Urban by default in the standard EM constructors; PAI on request per region); the fluctuation model is a model choice to vary, not a constant
rules.read: the SetFluctuationType call of the chosen EM constructor and /process/em/AddPAIRegion (particle, region, PAI or PAIphoton)

rules.concern: a deposit in a layer thinner than the electron range at the production cut is cut dependent (delta rays above the cut are tracked and may escape); the reference example of a 20 um silicon layer sets a 7 um cut
rules.read: the /run/setCut values of geant4:examples/extended/electromagnetic/TestEm5/TestEm5.in (7 um for 20 um Si) and the cut table the run prints

source.document: geant4:examples/extended/electromagnetic/TestEm5/TestEm5.in (/run/setCut 7 um before the 20 um Silicon run)

rules.concern: the EM constructors differ in models and options; option 4 is described by its author as the best standard and low-energy models with the most advanced options for precise simulation at low and intermediate energies
rules.read: the header comment and ConstructProcess of the chosen constructor

rules.concern: EM parameter commands (/process/em, /process/msc, /process/eLoss) exist only after an EM constructor has called G4EmParameters::SetDefaults, i.e. after the physics list is built, and must precede /run/initialize
rules.read: the constructor of the chosen EM constructor (param->SetDefaults()); layered_sim applies the spec's commands at that point and records them verbatim

rules.concern: G4StepLimiterPhysics attaches G4UserSpecialCuts to every particle; a track killed by it has its kinetic energy booked as a local deposit (ProposeLocalEnergyDeposit) and a killed e+ does not annihilate: the energy balance and any deposit observable must account for it

QGSP_BIC uses the Binary cascade only for protons and neutrons up to 1.5 GeV (Bertini from 1 GeV); for pions below 12 GeV and for nucleons between 1.5 and 12 GeV it uses the same models as FTFP_BERT (Bertini, the shared 3-6 GeV transition, then FTFP), so comparing the two lists there gives a false zero difference
rules.read: the transition energies of both hadronic constructors

source.document: geant4:source/physics_lists/constructors/hadron_inelastic/src/G4HadronPhysicsQGSP_BIC.cc (maxBIC_proton = maxBIC_neutron = 1.5 GeV, minBERT 1 GeV); geant4:source/physics_lists/constructors/hadron_inelastic/src/G4HadronPhysicsQGSP_BERT.cc and G4HadronPhysicsFTFP_BERT.cc; geant4:source/processes/hadronic/util/src/G4HadronicParameters.cc (FTF-cascade transition 3 to 6 GeV, QGS-FTF transition 12 to 25 GeV)

rules.concern: an unset dataset variable does not necessarily fail: G4FindDataDir searches GEANT4_DATA_DIR, the install data directory, /usr/local, /usr and /cvmfs/geant4.cern.ch and may silently use another copy; the run must record the resolved paths
rules.read: G4FindDataDir and the dataset list of the build

rules.concern: G4PVReplica does not override CheckOverlaps, so replicated volumes are never overlap-checked; /geometry/test/run is a sampled check
with secondary biasing the deposit is weighted but a leakage sum that ignores weights is not; TestEm3 run 1 does not close its energy balance
rules.read: TestEm3 run 1 (/process/em/setSecBiasing) and how the observable applies track weights

rules.concern: the Bethe mean rate is accurate to a few percent only for 0.1 <~ beta gamma <~ 1000; outside it the stopping-power benchmark is not applicable
rules.read: RPP 2024 Passage of particles through matter, Bethe equation

source.document: PDG RPP 2024, Passage of particles through matter (pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-passage-particles-matter.pdf)

rules.concern: electromagnetic shower observables depend on the production cut and the EM constructor, and leakage is energy leaving the world: unless split by face it includes the albedo (backscatter) and lateral escape; an escaping e+ carries its 2 m_e c^2 (TestEm3 convention); the PDG longitudinal profile is a fit to EGS4 showers (1-100 GeV) and supports only a sanity check, so a reference for leakage needs published data
rules.read: TestEm3 TrackingAction (leakage definition) and RPP 2024 Eqs. 34.34-34.36; layered_sim leak_rear_MeV, leak_front_MeV, leak_lateral_MeV

source.document: geant4:examples/extended/electromagnetic/TestEm3/src/TrackingAction.cc (leakage, 2 m_e c^2 added for an escaping e+); PDG RPP 2024, Passage of particles through matter, Eqs. 34.34-34.36

rules.concern: Geant4 asks users to cite its reference papers (the run banner of 11.4.3 prints them); a written result cites the Geant4 papers, the version and the documents relied on from a literature record, never from memory
rules.read: the run banner printed by G4RunManagerKernel and hep-citations primary-sources-and-version-checks (Geant4 row)

source.document: geant4:source/run/src/G4RunManagerKernel.cc (banner listing NIM A 506 (2003) 250-303, IEEE-TNS 53 (2006) 270-278, NIM A 835 (2016) 186-225)
